localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium
abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure
small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery

concepts.why: The abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right, and abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship are characteristic of intestinal malrotation.

The localized tenderness in the right lower abdomen and hypogastrium, positive McBurney’s sign, rebound tenderness, and elevated white-cell count are consistent with acute appendicitis, although the normal appearance of the appendix on imaging reduces the likelihood.

The abdominal pain, nausea, and localized tenderness, combined with the abnormal positioning of the small-bowel loops, could suggest intussusception, although the lack of clear evidence of bowel obstruction or ischemia reduces the likelihood.

The abnormal positioning of the small-bowel loops and the abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship could suggest a volvulus of the small intestine, which may be related to the intestinal malrotation.
The clustering of small-bowel loops and the abnormal positioning of the transverse colon and right colic flexure could suggest an internal hernia, which may be related to the intestinal malrotation.
The abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship and the appendix appearing normal suggest midgut volvulus.

rationales.F09: Abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure is indicative of malrotation of the intestine.
rationales.F10: Small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right is consistent with malrotation of the intestine and volvulus.
rationales.F11: Abnormal superior mesenteric artery-vein relationship is a key feature of malrotation of the intestine.
rationales.F12: Normal appearance of the appendix makes appendicitis less likely.
